story: In the beginning, the creator god was alone, a giant white in form, while darkness and primordial water covered the whole earth. Feeling intense pain in his stomach, he vomited up the sun, moon, and stars. The sun's heat and light evaporated the covering waters, forming clouds, and in time dry hills emerged from the water. He vomited again, bringing forth nine animals: a leopard, an eagle, a crocodile, a fish, a tortoise, a black leopard-like creature, a white heron, a scarab, and a goat. He also vomited many men, one of whom was white like himself and was set to serve as god upon the earth. The nine animals then created the world's other creatures: the heron made all flying birds except one, the crocodile made snakes and the iguana, the goat brought forth horned animals, the scarab made insects, and the fish-creature made all fish. Three of the creator's sons then set out to finish creation. The first vomited white ants and died; the ants dug deep for dark soil to bury him, transforming the barren sands above. The second son created the first plant, from which came all trees, grasses, and flowers. The third made the last bird, the kite. The black leopard-like creature caused trouble, so the creator chased her into the sky, where she became the thunderbolt, leaving people without fire until he taught them to make it from trees. Once creation was complete and peaceful, the creator gave it to mankind and withdrew into the heavens. Meanwhile, a woman of the waters lived in the east, and her son became the first king of the people.
